newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan takes second delivery of Mirage jets.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan takes second delivery of Mirage jets.

text.p: Taiwan has taken delivery of a further five French-made Mirage 2000 warplanes as part of moves to strengthen itself in the face of rival China's military modernisation, state television reported on Friday.
It showed the arrival of the second batch of Mirage 2000s from France in eastern Hualien harbour late on Thursday, bringing the total number of Mirages on the island to 10.
Taiwan took delivery of two U.S.-made F-16 warplanes in April.
Taiwan has said it needs the 60 Mirage and 150 F-16 fighters it bought in the early 1990s to counter a steady modernisation of China's three-million-strong People's Liberation Army.
China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, blasted the United States for selling the F-16s to Taiwan, saying the move seriously harmed relations.
Beijing vows to retake the island eventually -- by force if necessary.
China mounted eight months of war games and missile tests near Taiwan in 1995 and 1996 in what it acknowledged was an attempt to dissuade the island from pursuing independence.
Under pressure from Beijing, Paris agreed in 1994 to halt new arms sales to Taiwan, though it planned to complete delivery of the Mirage fighters ordered in 1992.
China sees any sales of advanced foreign military technology to Taiwan as an encroachment on its sovereignty.
